prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Code · Config options with long tokens (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Option" · longest unbreakable word 131px · one-line width 131px
  col 2: header "Default" · longest unbreakable word 90px · one-line width 334px
  col 3: header "Example" · longest unbreakable word 537px · one-line width 537px
  col 4: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 501px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A reference/config-option table: readers look up one option by name and then check its default, see a realistic example value, and read what it does. It is scanned by row, not compared across rows, so row identity (the option key) must be findable instantly.","reading":"Vertical scan down column 1 to find the key, then a short rightward hop to Default/Example and finally the prose Description. Option and Default form the 'lookup' pair read together; Example and Description form the 'explanation' pair. Rows must read as units, so keys should not break and the long code tokens should not be shredded into unreadable fragments.","groups":["Option + Default: the identity/lookup pair, read together in one glance","Example + Description: the explanation pair, both wide and both needing generous width","Option alone must lead: it is the scan anchor and the only column whose values are all short, uniform identifiers"],"keep_intact":["Option keys (server.port, cache.ttlSeconds, auth.jwksUri) — the row's handle; 131px + 21px padding","Default values (8080, 300, —) — short, cheap to keep whole","The Example token is a single 537px unbreakable string: it can never be whole at 360px, so it must either be given a scrolling width or deliberately split"],"may_wrap":["Description — ordinary prose, wraps cleanly at any width and absorbs height","Default's rare long value (334px one-liner) can wrap rather than steal width from Option","Example may be split only if the design accepts scroll or a fragment; it should not be squeezed into a 60px sliver where it becomes noise"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[152,72,66,69],"idea":"Hard fit inside 360px: give Option exactly its 131px so every key stays whole, and let Default, Example and Description all wrap or split in the narrow remainder — no horizontal scrolling, but the Example token and the Description become cramped fragments."},{"name":"B","widths":[152,111,558,220],"idea":"Never break a value: Option and Default get their full unbreakable widths and Example gets all 537px so the code token stays on one line, accepting a ~1040px table that the reader scrolls horizontally for the two right-hand columns."},{"name":"C","widths":[152,96,290,190],"idea":"Deliberate compromise: Option intact and Default nearly intact, Example given a wide 290px slot so the token breaks into at most a couple of readable chunks instead of a sliver, and Description wide enough to wrap at a comfortable measure, with a moderate scroll for the right half."}]}
